records.headline: Special weather statement
records.description:
Prolonged, heavy rainfall is possible.

Locations: southern New Brunswick.

Potential rainfall: 40 to 70 mm.

Time span: this evening until Sunday night.

Remarks: A slow-moving weather system is expected to bring a period of prolonged rainfall which may become heavy at times. Thundershowers may develop over some areas, producing locally heavier rainfall, especially tonight into Saturday morning.

There is some uncertainty as to where the highest rainfall amounts will occur, but the potential exists for significant totals over some locations, especially along the Bay of Fundy.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to NBstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #NBStorm.

records.headline: Special weather statement
records.description:
What:
Moderate to strong gusty winds.

When:
Now through late this evening.

Where:
- South Cariboo
- South Thompson
- Fraser Canyon - north including Lillooet
- Yellowhead (near West Twin Creek)

Additional information:
A strong low pressure system approaching the B.C. coast is bringing a prolonged period of southeast winds with gusts ranging from 60-80 km/h to the B.C. interior. These southeast winds will peak this morning with the exception of South Thompson and Lilooet whose winds will peak this afternoon. Winds may ease slightly this afternoon before an incoming cold front will bring a strong push of southwest winds, with gusts potentially reaching 90 km/h between South Thompson and Quesnel. 

Another potentially strong storm is set to follow on Saturday evening. 

Local utility outages are possible. Parks and forests may sustain damage. Secure loose objects.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to BCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #BCStorm.

records.description:
What:
Moderate to strong gusty winds.

When:
Now till late this evening.

Where:
- Nicola
- Coquihalla Highway - Hope to Merritt
- Coquihalla Highway - Merritt to Kamloops
- Okanagan Connector - Merritt to Kelowna


Additional information:
A strong low pressure system is approaching the B.C. coast and is bringing a prolonged period of southeast winds with gusts ranging from 60-80 km/h to the B.C. Interior and highway passes. records.area: Vancouver Island Coastline from Bamfield to Clo-oose
records.headline: Coastal flooding statement
records.description:
This statement is in effect for parts of the coast due to the following hazard(s): 
- Higher than normal water levels

Elevated ocean water levels accompanied by strong winds and waves are expected, exceeding highest astronomical tide.

What:
-Possible coastal flooding due to storm surge coinciding with high tide.

When:
-Saturday near noon (10 am to 2 pm) and Sunday near noon (10 am to 2 pm).

Where:
-Coastlines along west Vancouver Island.

Additional Information:
A deep low-pressure system will track across the region this weekend, bringing strong south to southeast winds to Vancouver Island before shifting to southwesterly winds. These southwest winds will generate large waves along the west coast of Vancouver Island, particularly on Sunday. The timing of the strong onshore winds and high waves with high tide may result in water levels potentially exceeding the highest astronomical tide.

Minor coastal flooding is likely along exposed shorelines especially in the low-lying areas.

Roads and walkways maybe difficult to navigate due to flooding and/or debris, such as driftwood and rocks. 

Coastal erosion is possible in sensitive areas, such as tidal flats, estuaries, dunes, beaches and barrier islands.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to BCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #BCStorm.

records.headline: Wind warning
records.description:
Damaging winds are expected.

What:
A strong sudden push of southwest wind with gusts ranging from 80-100 km/h. Localized gusts of 100-120 km/h are possible.

When:
Tonight for the Central Interior. Overnight for the Peace District.

Where:
- Lakes District
- Stuart-Nechako
- Prince George
- North Cariboo
- Williston (Including Pine Pass)
- McGregor
- Peace District

Additional information:
A very strong low pressure system will trek across the B.C interior this evening. As the low passes across the region, a very strong push of wind is expected to follow the low, which will produce a sudden shift of wind direction and gusts of up to 100 km/h. This push of wind will first impact the Lakes District, including Ootsa Lake and Burns Lake, late this afternoon and will continue eastwards towards Stuart-Nechako, Prince George, Mackenzie, and the McGregor region respectively throughout the evening. The strong wind push should reach the Peace District just after midnight. Winds should ease within a few hours of the strong push occurring, and moderate winds will continue this afternoon before the push arrives.

Damage to roofs, fences, branches or soft shelters is possible.

Stay away from fallen power lines. Be prepared to adapt your driving for changing conditions. Prepare for possible disruptions to transportation, services, and utilities.

Wind warnings are issued when there is a significant risk of damaging winds.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to BCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #BCStorm.

records.headline: Wind warning
records.description:
Damaging winds are expected.

When: Saturday morning to late Saturday afternoon.

Where: North Vancouver Island.

Remarks:
Another storm, currently located over the Eastern Pacific, will approach the B.C. coast on Saturday. An associated frontal system will bring southeast winds gusting to 110 km/h to the region Saturday morning.

After the passage of the front, winds will ease below warning criteria late Saturday afternoon but remain gusty through Saturday night.

Local utility outages are possible. High-sided vehicles will be pushed around by the wind. Disruptions to services and travel are possible.

Secure loose objects.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to BCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #BCStorm.

records.headline: Rainfall warning
records.description:
Rain, at times heavy, is expected.

Locations: Bay of Fundy coastline.

Total rainfall: 50 to 80 mm, with locally higher amounts in thundershowers.

Time span: this evening until Sunday evening.

Remarks: Heavy rain with embedded thundershowers will move in off the Bay of Fundy this evening. Rainfall rates of 10 to 20 mm per hour may occur over some locations. Rain will begin to taper off through the day on Sunday.

Allow extra time for travel.

Rainfall warnings are issued when significant impacts are expected due to rainfall amounts.

records.headline: Blizzard warning
records.description:
Blizzard conditions with potentially damaging winds and persistent visibility near zero in snow and blowing snow.

When: Tonight. 

Where: Dempster Highway near the Richardson Mountains.

Remarks:
A stationary ridge over the Beaufort Sea combined with a low pressure system over the Gulf of Alaska is creating favourable conditions for strong easterly winds along the Dempster Highway.

Winds gusts up to 90 km/h, together with falling snow and snow already on the ground, will result in blizzard conditions and near zero visibility. Winds are forecast to ease early Saturday but remain gusty through the day, as blowing snow and reduced visibility can still be expected.

Travel will likely be hazardous in some locations. Road closures are possible.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to YTstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #YTStorm.

records.headline: Snowfall warning
records.description:
Snowfall, with total amounts of 30 to 40 cm is expected.

Snow will begin tonight as a low pressure system approaches southern Baffin Island. Steady heavy snowfall will continue through Saturday and into Sunday morning as the system stalls over the area. 

Total snowfall amounts in the range of 30 to 40 cm are expected by the time snow ends Sunday afternoon, and potentially higher amounts are possible with onshore winds off the open water of Cumberland Sound.

Visibility will likely be reduced at times.

Prepare for quickly changing and deteriorating travel conditions. Take frequent breaks and avoid strain when clearing snow.

Snowfall warnings are issued when significant impacts are expected due to snowfall accumulations.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to NUstorm@ec.gc.ca, call 1-800-239-0484 or post reports on social media using #NUStorm.

records.headline: Flood Warning issued November 6 at 8:39PM EST until November 6 at 10:45PM EST by NWS Boston/Norton MA
records.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...East Central Bristol County in southeastern
Massachusetts...
Southeastern Plymouth County in southeastern Massachusetts...

* WHEN...Until 1045 PM EST.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 839 PM EST, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly
in the warned area. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 1.5 inches are possible in
the warned area.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
New Bedford, Plymouth, Dartmouth, Marion, Wareham, Fairhaven,
Acushnet, Freetown, Mattapoisett and Rochester.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
records.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

records.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued November 6 at 5:22PM MST until November 6 at 11:15PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
records.description:
FFWFGZ

The National Weather Service in Flagstaff has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Coconino County in north central Arizona...
Yavapai County in west central Arizona...

* Until 1115 PM MST.

* At 522 PM MST, National Weather Service Flagstaff Doppler radar
indicated heavy rainfall in the West Clear Creek drainage from
earlier thunderstorms. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to
begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
normally dry washes, urban areas, highways, streets and
underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Verde Lakes, Hanging Garden, Indian Maiden Falls and West Clear
Creek Wilderness.

This includes State Route 260 between mile markers 225 and 229.

This includes the following recreation areas and campgrounds...
Clear Creek Group Campgrounds.

This includes the following swimming holes...
Bull Pen Day Use Area, West Clear Creek near the campground and
Indian Maiden Falls.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Verde River near the confluence of West Clear Creek and West Clear
Creek.
records.instruction:
Flooding of washes and creeks will occur, some dirt roads will become
muddy and impassable. Paved roads and underpasses could become
flooded as well.

records.headline: Marine Weather Statement issued November 6 at 7:44PM AST by NWS San Juan PR
records.description:

Anegada Passage east of Virgin Gorda and Saint Croix south to 17N...
Coastal waters east of Puerto Rico, around Vieques, and around and
just north of Culebra and Saint John...
Caribbean waters of Puerto Rico from 10 NM to 17N, including the
coastal waters of Saint Croix...

* At 744 PM AST, Doppler radar indicated strong thunderstorms,
capable of producing winds to around 30 knots and possible
waterspouts. These strong thunderstorms were located across the
Caribbean offshore waters and the Anegada Passage, approaching
coastal waters of St. Croix, moving north at 15 knots.

Mainly open waters of Anegada Passage east of Virgin Gorda and
Saint Croix south to 17N, Coastal waters east of Puerto Rico,
around Vieques, and around and just north of Culebra and Saint John
and Caribbean waters of Puerto Rico from 10 NM to 17N, including
the coastal waters of Saint Croix.
records.instruction:
Report severe weather to the Coast Guard or nearest law enforcement
agency. They will relay your report to the National Weather Service
office.

Mariners can expect gusty winds to around 30 knots, locally higher
waves, lightning strikes, heavy downpours, and waterspouts. Boaters
should seek safe harbor immediately until these storms pass.

records.headline: Flood Warning issued November 6 at 4:28PM MST until November 7 at 11:00AM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
records.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by upstream dam releases continues.

* WHERE...Maricopa County in south central Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 1100 AM MST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of the Salt River below Granite Reef Dam is
occurring. Flooding of low water crossings across the Salt River
upstream of Tempe Town Lake, including McKellips Road, is
occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 427 PM MST, dam operators reported around 1400 cfs was being
released from Granite Reef Dam. Additionally, a streamflow gauge
downstream of Granite Reef Dam measured a flow around 2000 cfs.
Flooding due to a dam floodgate release will continue.
- Flooding is occurring along the Salt River.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Salt River between Granite Reef Dam and Tempe Town Lake.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
records.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Flooding is occurring. It is important to know where you are relative
to streams, rivers, or creeks. Campers and hikers should avoid
streams or creeks.

records.area: Santa Clarita Valley; Western Santa Monica Mountains Recreational Area; Eastern Santa Monica Mountains Recreational Area; Santa Susana Mountains; Western San Gabriel Mountains and Highway 14 Corridor
records.headline: Red Flag Warning issued November 6 at 3:14PM PST until November 7 at 6:00PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
records.description:
...RISK FOR RAPID FIRE GROWTH AND EXTREME FIRE BEHAVIOR WITH ANY
NEW FIRE STARTS, ESPECIALLY LATE TONIGHT THROUGH SATURDAY...

.Weak to moderate Santa Ana winds will be on the increase,
peaking on Saturday. During the peak, gusts of 30 to 45 mph will
be common in the typical wind-prone areas of Los Angeles and
Ventura Counties. Meanwhile, the air will warm and dry, with
minimum humidities in the 8 to 20 percent range common by
Saturday. Fuels remain critically dry despite some minor greenup
from recent rains. There is a high risk for fast-moving fires
where the plants are driest and the winds are strongest, which
this targeted Red Flag Warning addresses.

* AFFECTED AREA...Santa Clarita Valley, Western Santa Monica
Mountains Recreational Area, Eastern Santa Monica Mountains
Recreational Area, Santa Susana Mountains and Western San
Gabriel Mountains and Highway 14 Corridor.

* TIMING...From 2 AM to 6 PM PST Saturday.

* WINDS...Northeast 20 to 30 mph with gusts up to 45 mph.
Isolated gusts 45 to 55 mph in most favored locations.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...Minimums of 8 to 20 percent. Poor
overnight recoveries.

* IMPACTS...If fire ignition occurs, conditions are favorable
for extreme fire behavior which would threaten life and
property.
records.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions
are either occurring now, or will shortly. Use extreme caution
with anything that can spark a wildfire. Residents near wildland
interfaces should be prepared to evacuate if a wildfire breaks
out. See readyforwildfire.org and wildfirerisk.org for
information.

records.area: Coastal Del Norte; Northern Coastal Humboldt; Southwestern Humboldt; Coastal Mendocino
records.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 6 at 2:30PM PST until November 8 at 10:00PM PST by NWS Eureka CA
records.description:
* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, increased threat of
sneaker waves expected. For the High Surf Advisory, large
breaking waves 22-24 feet.

* WHERE...Coastal Del Norte, Northern Coastal Humboldt,
Southwestern Humboldt and Coastal Mendocino Counties.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, until midnight PST
tonight. For the High Surf Advisory, from 4 AM to 10 PM PST
Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous surf conditions and localized beach
erosion. Beachcombing is highly discouraged! Large, unexpected
waves can sweep across the beach without warning, sweeping
people into the sea from rocks, jetties, and beaches. These
sneaker waves can also move large objects such as logs,
crushing anyone caught underneath.
records.instruction:
Don't be fooled by an ocean that looks calm.  There can be
30 minutes of small waves before a sneaker wave strikes.  Avoid
rocks and jetties. Avoid steep beaches.  Stay much farther back
from the water and never turn your back on the ocean.

Large breaking waves along the coast will lead to increased wave
run-up on beaches with waves topping and washing over large rocks
and jetties. These large waves can be erratic and unpredictable.
Use extra caution near the surf zone as these large waves will be
capable of sweeping people into the frigid and turbulent ocean
water. Mariners traversing the bar are urged to exercise extreme
caution or stay in port until the threat subsides. Please contact
the U.S. Coast Guard for information regarding harbor and bar
closures.

records.area: Northern Washington Coast; Grays Harbor County Coast
records.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 6 at 1:55PM PST until November 8 at 10:00PM PST by NWS Seattle WA
records.description:
* WHAT...Large breaking waves along the coast.

* WHERE...Northern Washington Coast and Grays Harbor County
Coast zones.

* WHEN...From 4 AM to 10 PM PST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Large breaking waves can knock people off their feet,
move driftwood and debris, and crash over rocks and jetties.
People can be injured or drown while observing the ocean.
Localized beach and coastal erosion is expected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Caution should be used when in or near the
water, especially those who will be participating in razor clam
digging.
records.instruction:
Never turn your back on the ocean and keep children and pets
close. Know the tides and forecast conditions. Follow warning
signs and respect barriers.

records.area: Clatsop County Coast; Tillamook County Coast; Central Coast of Oregon; South Washington Coast
records.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued November 6 at 12:57PM PST until November 8 at 4:00AM PST by NWS Portland OR
records.description:
* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement on the beaches, sneaker
waves possible. For the High Surf Advisory on the beaches, large
waves, hazardous surf conditions, and sneaker waves. Breakers
up to 28 feet.

* WHERE...North and Central Coast of Oregon, and South
Washington Coast.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, through late Saturday
night. For the High Surf Advisory, from 4 AM to 10 PM PST
Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Destructive waves may wash over beaches, jetties, and
other structures unexpectedly. People can be swept off rocks and
jetties and drown while observing high surf. Minor beach erosion
may damage coastal properties and buildings. Higher than normal
water run-up is expected on beaches and low-lying shoreline due
to sneaker waves. Sneaker waves can suddenly knock people off
of their feet and quickly pull them into the frigid ocean which
may lead to serious injury or drowning.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Caution should be used when in or near
the water, especially those who will be razor clamming. Keep
children and pets away from the surf zone. Keep off of
jetties, rocks and logs near the surf zone. If you see someone
swept into the sea do not swim in after them. Call 911 and
keep an eye on them until help arrives.
records.instruction:
A High Surf Advisory means that high surf will affect beaches,
producing rip currents, sneaker waves and beach erosion. Stay
well back from the water's edge and be alert for exceptionally
high waves.

Keep away from large logs on the beach. Water running up on the
beach can easily lift or roll logs which can injure or kill
someone caught in their path.

Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous swimming conditions.

records.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued November 6 at 10:08AM PST until November 9 at 10:00PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
records.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up to 1.6 ft of
inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Beach Hazards
Statement, an increased risk for sneaker waves and strong rip
currents with breaking waves of 12 to 16 ft expected.

* WHERE...San Francisco.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 PM PST Friday
November 13. For the Beach Hazards Statement, until Monday
evening.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without warning,
pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tide gauge, high tide
is expected to be: 1.6 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW) at 9:38 AM
Saturday 11/7, 1.6 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW) at 10:06 AM
Sunday 11/8, 1.6 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW) at 10:35 AM
Monday 11/9, 1.5 ft above normal (7.3 ft MLLW) at 11:04 AM
Tuesday 11/10, 1.4 ft above normal (7.2 ft MLLW) at 11:35 AM
Wednesday 11/11, 1.4 ft above normal (7.2 ft MLLW) at 12:10 PM
Thursday 11/12, 1.2 ft above normal (7.0 ft MLLW) at 12:49 PM
Friday 11/13. These predictions include up to 1.5 ft of surge
that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat.
High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the
Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.
records.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Stay off of jetties, piers, rocks, and other waterside
infrastructure. Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous surf
and NEVER turn your back on the ocean. Monitor local weather,
surf and tide forecasts at www.weather.gov/mtr.

inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Beach Hazards
Statement, an increased risk for sneaker waves and strong rip
currents with breaking waves of 12 to 16 ft expected.

* WHERE...San Francisco.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 PM PST Friday
November 13. For the Beach Hazards Statement, until Monday
evening.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without warning,
pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tide gauge, high tide
is expected to be: 1.6 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW) at 9:38 AM
Saturday 11/7, 1.6 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW) at 10:06 AM
Sunday 11/8, 1.6 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW) at 10:35 AM
Monday 11/9, 1.5 ft above normal (7.3 ft MLLW) at 11:04 AM
Tuesday 11/10, 1.4 ft above normal (7.2 ft MLLW) at 11:35 AM
Wednesday 11/11, 1.4 ft above normal (7.2 ft MLLW) at 12:10 PM
Thursday 11/12, 1.2 ft above normal (7.0 ft MLLW) at 12:49 PM
Friday 11/13. These predictions include up to 1.5 ft of surge
that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat.
High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the
Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.
records.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Stay off of jetties, piers, rocks, and other waterside
infrastructure. Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous surf
and NEVER turn your back on the ocean. Monitor local weather,
surf and tide forecasts at www.weather.gov/mtr.

records.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 7 at 3:57AM ChST until November 7 at 4:00PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
records.description:
* WHAT...Large breaking waves of 7 to 9 feet and dangerous rip
currents.

* WHERE...For the High Surf Advisory, north facing reefs of the
Marianas. For the High Rip Current Risk, north and east facing
reefs.

* WHEN...Until 4 PM ChST this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Elevated northeast trade swell, a smaller
long-period north swell, and a north to northwest swell from
Tropical Depression 31W continues to generate hazardous surf
along north facing reefs and a high risk of rip currents along
north and east facing reefs of the Marianas through this
afternoon.
records.instruction:
Rip currents will be life threatening. Inexperienced swimmers
should remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents will be life threatening. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

records.headline: High Wind Watch issued November 6 at 10:56AM MST until November 8 at 8:00PM MST by NWS Great Falls MT
records.description:
* WHAT...For the High Wind Warning, southwest winds 30 to 50 mph with
gusts up to 80 mph. For the High Wind Watch, west winds 30 to 50
mph with gusts up to 85 mph possible.

* WHERE...East Glacier Park Region Zone, and Eastern Glacier, Western
Toole, and Central Pondera, Northern High Plains, and Southern High
Plains.

* WHEN...For the High Wind Warning, until 9 AM MST Saturday. For the
High Wind Watch, from Sunday morning through Sunday evening.

* IMPACTS...Travel will be very difficult, especially for high
profile vehicles or for those towing light weight trailers.
Isolated power outages possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Two periods of strong winds continue through
the weekend, with a break from these strong winds occurring from
the late morning hours on Saturday through the mid-morning hours on
Sunday. The most intense periods of winds are expected to occur
tonight with the first round, and then during the afternoon hours
on Sunday with the second round.
records.instruction:
People are urged to secure loose objects that could be blown around
or damaged by the wind.

Monitor the latest forecasts and warnings for updates.

records.area: San Luis Obispo County Beaches; Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches
records.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 6 at 1:39AM PST until November 9 at 10:00PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
records.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, moderate coastal
flooding expected. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking
waves of 10 to 16 feet with dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara
County Central Coast Beaches.

* WHEN...Until 10 PM PST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time
of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths,
and harbor walkways. Moderate beach erosion is likely.
Isolated damage is unlikely but possible. There is an
increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull
swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can
cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize
small boats near shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tides of 7.1 to 7.4 feet (MLLW) are
expected each morning.
records.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Do
NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay
near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.

records.area: Catalina and Santa Barbara Islands; Santa Barbara County Southwestern Coast; Santa Barbara County Southeastern Coast; Ventura County Beaches; Malibu Coast; Los Angeles County Beaches
records.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued November 6 at 1:39AM PST until November 10 at 12:00PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
records.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents and breaking waves due to elevated
surf up to 4 to 6 feet expected. Surf will likely increase
around Monday for the Ventura Coasts.

* WHERE...Catalina and Santa Barbara Islands, Santa Barbara
County Southwestern Coast, Santa Barbara County Southeastern
Coast, Ventura County Beaches, Malibu Coast and Los Angeles
County Beaches.

* WHEN...Through Tuesday morning.

* IMPACTS...There is an increased risk of ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Waves can
wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats
nearshore. Pooling of sea water is possible around high tide
at beach and harbor areas that is uncommon with normal tidal
ranges. Enhanced beach erosion is also possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tides of 7.2 to 7.6 feet (MLLW) are
expected each morning. Surf and coastal flooding impacts peak on
Monday, when a High Surf Advisory and Coastal Flood Advisory is
likely to be issued for the Ventura Coasts. For the remainder of
the coasts, it is possible that a Coastal Flood Advisory is
needed for Monday as well.
records.instruction:
Remain out of the water due to hazardous swimming conditions, or
stay near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly
in such conditions, stay off the rocks.

records.area: Coastal Volusia; Coastal Indian River; Coastal St. Lucie; Coastal Martin; Mainland Northern Brevard; Northern Brevard Barrier Islands; Mainland Southern Brevard; Southern Brevard Barrier Islands
records.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 6 at 1:25AM EST until November 8 at 2:00AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
records.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents expected.

* WHERE...The beaches of Volusia, Brevard, Indian River, Saint
Lucie and Martin counties.

* WHEN...Through late Saturday night.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
records.instruction:
Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

records.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 6 at 3:18PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
records.description:
A developing tropical disturbance, Invest 99W, is quickly approaching
the islands of the northern CNMI. The Joint Typhoon Warning Center
(JTWC) has issued a Tropical Cyclone Formation Alert (TCFA) for 99W.
This means that development into a significant tropical cyclone is
likely within the next 24 hours. What this means for the northern
CNMI of Alamagan, Pagan and Agrihan is that you can expect an
increase in showers and thunderstorms with strong gusty winds as 99W
moves past. Invest 99W is currently not expected to move through the
northern CNMI stronger than a Tropical Depression. However, as with
all tropical cyclones, this could change.

Invest 99W is currently moving fairly quickly, which is a good thing
for the northern CNMI. At the current speed, 99W looks to pass
through the region near Alamagan Saturday morning or early afternoon,
not becoming a Tropical Storm until later in the day, west of the
islands. Invest 99W will be monitored over the next 24 hours for any
significant changes in expectations and the residents of the
northern CNMI should continue to monitor forecasts for any changes to
the current expectations. For now, prepare for increasing rainfall,
with isolated thunderstorms and strong gusty winds within the heavier
showers. Only 1 to 2 inches of rainfall is expected, with gusts up
to 40 mph possible.

For more information on Invest 99W, see bulletins issued by JTWC
under WMO header ABPW10 PGTW and WTPN21 PGTW.

records.headline: Flood Warning issued November 5 at 9:46PM MST until November 7 at 2:00PM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
records.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by upstream dam release continues.

* WHERE...Maricopa County in south central Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 200 PM MST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is occurring. Low-water crossings are
inundated with water and may not be passable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 940 PM MST, upstream floodgate release from Tempe Town Lake
and continued releases from Granite Reef Dam farther upstream has
lead to flooding in the warned area. A US Army Core of Engineers
streamflow gauge on the Gila River showed a flow near Old US 80
was around 8700 cfs and inflow into Painted Rock Reservoir was
around 15700 cfs.
- Flooding is occurring along the Salt and Gila Rivers.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Goodyear, Painted Rock Dam, Liberty, Phoenix International
Raceway and Arlington.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
records.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

records.area: East Midlands | East of England | London & South East England | West Midlands
records.headline: Areas of fog developing this evening and overnight, dense in places
records.description:
Clearing skies over southeast England this evening and overnight, which has already led to the development of mist and some patchy fog, is likely to allow increasingly widespread and in places dense fog to form. Visibility could fall as low as 100m in some places. The fog will gradually lift and clear to mist and haze during Saturday morning, persisting longest where visibilities are poorest early on.

For further details see https://www.metoffice.gov.uk/weather/warnings-and-advice/uk-warnings
records.instruction: Give yourself the best chance of avoiding delays by checking road conditions if driving, leaving extra journey time, or amending plans if necessary. Make sure you know how to switch on your fog lights, and check they are working before setting off on your journey. Bus and train services, as well as flights and ferry travel may also be affected; check for updates from your travel company and follow their advice.

records.headline: Yellow Thunderstorm, Snow warning · Borçka, Artvin
records.description: Aralıklı ve yerel olarak çok kuvvetli ve şiddetli (50-100 kg/m2)  sağanak ve yer yer  gök gürültülü sağanak yağış  bekleniyor. 1100 metre rakım üzerinde görülecek kar yağışlarının , zamanla soğumaya bağlı olarak 600 metre rakım üzeri yükseklerde de görüleceği ve  yer yer yoğun (20 cm üzeri)  olacağı tahmin ediliyor. Şiddetli yağışlarla birlikte  ulaşımda aksamalar, sel, su baskını,  heyelan, yükseklerde buzlanma ve don, tipi gibi olumsuzluklara karşı dikkatli ve tedbirli olunmalıdır.

Şiddetli yağışlarla birlikte  ulaşımda aksamalar, sel, su baskını,  heyelan, yükseklerde buzlanma ve don, tipi gibi olumsuzluklara karşı dikkatli ve tedbirli olunmalıdır.
